narrative: Material PL1__M60E8727 displays intermittent demand (55% active working days) with a very high coefficient of variation of 1.41, characteristic of a Negative Binomial demand process. Lead times are short but highly unstable (CV=0.83), amplifying safety stock requirements. An (r,Q) policy is recommended with safety stock set at 226 units to achieve the 95% service level; the order quantity of 3,233 is constrained by the 3,460-unit storage limit, which prevents deployment of the unconstrained EOQ of 6,132 units.
warnings: High demand variability: CV=1.41 exceeds 1.0 threshold
Intermittent demand: only 55.3% of working days have non-zero demand
Unstable lead times: CV=0.83 exceeds 0.6 threshold
Storage capacity binding: order_quantity capped at 3233 (unconstrained EOQ=6132); near-full utilisation at 99.98%

research_insights.selection_rationale: Given intermittent, high-CV demand and short but variable lead times, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is preferred over periodic review because it triggers replenishment as soon as inventory hits the reorder point, minimising stockout exposure during unpredictable demand spikes. The EOQ provides the cost-optimal order size subject to the storage cap.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is binding at 99.98% utilisation. The order quantity has been reduced from the unconstrained EOQ of 6,132 to 3,233 units, roughly doubling the number of annual orders and increasing annual ordering cost by ~89%. If demand spikes coincide with a replenishment cycle, the reduced order quantity may not fully replenish depleted stock, increasing effective stockout risk despite the 95% SS calculation.
